text: Every AI agent has the same flaw. It forgets. Crash it, or change its goal, and its reasoning is gone.
This is Second Shift. Its memory lives in MongoDB Atlas, not in the model. Claude designs each experiment on real brain signals, code measures it, and Jev files every insight away.
Now, watch. We kill the worker in the middle of the run. A new one rebuilds everything from Atlas, and picks up right where it fell. Nothing lost. Nothing repeated.
Then we change the rules. We wipe its context, and cut the electrodes from sixty four to nine. It already knows which results still count, and it keeps going.
Thirteen of thirteen reliability checks passed. Ten thousand memories, and every decision still fits in twelve hundred tokens.
Second Shift. Agents that never lose the plot.
